DayOff Mate (연차메이트) Without sign-in, records stay on your phone

DayOff Mate Privacy Policy

Effective November 28, 2026 (published November 27, 2026) · App: DayOff Mate (연차메이트) · Package com.blessingq.dayoffmate · Developer: JAEYOUNG LEE (blessingq)

This English version is a translation provided for convenience. If it differs from the Korean version, the Korean version prevails.

At a glance

  • If you use the app without signing in, your hire date, leave records and notes are stored only on your phone and never sent to the developer's servers.
  • If you sign in, your records are stored in Google Firebase (Seoul region) so you can continue on another phone and see days off with groups.
  • Groups only see what you choose to share. Notes, hire date and day adjustments are never shared.
  • The hourly pay and allowances you enter for estimated pay on the Work tab are stored only on this phone, never on our servers, in groups or in backups.
  • Calendar events are read and written only on your phone. Google Drive auto-backup is saved in your own Google Drive; the developer cannot receive or see it.
  • We send crash reports and usage statistics to fix bugs and improve features. Usage statistics do not use the advertising ID, are not linked to your account, and can be turned off in Settings.
  • The app shows one ad card at the bottom of the Home tab and one on the Work tab, and you can choose to watch an ad to open the year-end review. For this, Google processes device identifiers and related information (section 9). The iOS app does not ask to track you and shows only non-personalized ads.

JAEYOUNG LEE (blessingq, the “developer”) processes the personal information of people who use the mobile app DayOff Mate (연차메이트, package com.blessingq.dayoffmate, the “app”) in accordance with the Korean Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA) and related laws, and publishes this policy under Article 30 of PIPA. It applies to the Android app and the iOS app (including the Apple Watch app).

1. Purposes of processing

  1. Sign-up and account management: verifying sign-in (Kakao, Naver, Google; Apple on iOS), linking and unlinking several sign-in methods on one account, confirming you are 14 or older, recording consent to the Terms and the Privacy Policy, deleting accounts, answering inquiries and verifying identity
  2. Sync: storing your leave settings, records, day adjustments and settings in your account so you can use them on another phone. Also your work schedule, personal schedule, company calendar, half-day hours and comp time. Also extra shifts and events (dates you note down, such as weddings or birthdays)
  3. Groups: creating, inviting and joining groups, showing your days off to group members at the level you choose, finding common days off, and (if you allow it) letting people find you by your ID. Showing each day's shift type to groups where you turn on “Show my shift schedule”
  4. Plan a get-together (find a time with friends): letting a signed-in organizer create a plan, collecting the available times submitted by people who received the link (they don't need the app), and finding and setting a time that works for everyone
  5. Notifications: sending push notifications about group members' days off and join requests. Your own leave and expiry reminders (and event reminders) are scheduled on your phone and do not go through the server.
  6. Reliability and security: finding the cause of app crashes and server errors, checking requests come from the genuine app, preventing abuse (rate limits), remote configuration (maintenance notices, feature switches, updates to holiday data and help-line information)
  7. Improvement: per-feature usage statistics (when “Send usage statistics” is on)
  8. Advertising: ad cards on the Home and Work tabs and an optional rewarded ad for the year-end review (only when you tap it), to keep the app free
  9. User protection: handling reports and violations of the Terms

2. Information we process and how we collect it

We process the following personal information without consent under Article 15(1)(4) of PIPA (entering into and performing a contract): sign-in provider identifier, app user ID, email address (Google sign-in), sign-in method, sign-up time, the times you confirmed being 14+ and gave consent, server access and error logs, crash reports, and app check information. You can turn off usage statistics in the app settings, and delete or reset the advertising ID used for ads as described in section 9.

2.1 Without signing in

There is no account and nothing personal is stored on the developer's servers. Your hire date, leave basis, workplace size, workplace type, weekend setting, leave records (type, date, AM/PM, hours, note), day adjustments and app settings are stored only on your phone. Section 2.4 (automatically generated information) applies whether or not you sign in.

Extra shifts (date, name, start time, hours, color, note) and extra shift types, and events (title, date, number of days, time, yearly repeat, color, note, reminder timing). You can link Kakao, Naver and Google (and Apple on iOS) sign-in to one account; signing in with any linked method opens the same account. When you link a method, we store the identifier received from that provider in the account; when you unlink it, we delete that identifier. We never look up or merge separate accounts by email or name, and we do not link a sign-in that another account already uses.

Your email is used only for account management (answering inquiries, verifying identity). It is never shown in the app or to groups and never used for marketing. The app does not save the provider's name or profile photo as app data. However, for Google and Apple sign-in, the authentication service (Firebase Authentication) may keep the basic profile passed by the provider (name, profile photo URL) in its sign-in record; the app does not use it on screen or in groups.

2.3 When you use groups

  • Nickname (required, entered when you sign up), ID (set automatically when you sign up; it can't be changed), whether others may find you by ID (on by default; you can turn it off in Settings)
  • Group name and type, members and roles, join time, pending join requests
  • Per-group sharing level (days only / with leave types), whether to show remaining leave, per-group notification setting, whether to show your shift schedule (off by default)
  • Shared information shown to the group (dates off with full day/AM/PM/partial; depending on your level, leave type and hours; if enabled, remaining leave and its as-of date; if “Show my shift schedule” is on, each day's day off or shift type, with the shift types' names and colors)
  • Invitations sent and received, block list, group activity log (joined, left, removed, owner changed, including nicknames)
  • Reports, if you file one

2.3.1 When you plan a get-together

  • Organizer (signed-in user): plan name, length, expected number of people, candidate dates and time range, the organizer's available times (30-minute slots) or “none of these times work”, the time that was set, and status
  • People who answer through the link (they don't need to use the app): the name they enter, their available times (30-minute slots) or “none of these times work”, and when they answered
  • So that an answer can be changed or deleted only from the same browser, the answer page creates a random edit key and keeps it in that browser's storage (localStorage); the server stores only a hash of the key as the answer ID. The last name entered is also kept only in that browser.
  • A hash of the IP address, to prevent repeated requests (the address itself is not stored)
  • Pre-selecting the organizer's free times happens only on the phone; shift types, plan names and other days' schedules are not sent to the server.

2.5 When you contact us, send feedback or ask for deletion

Your email address, the content of your message, and the details you give to verify your identity: sign-in method, sign-in email, nickname, ID, group names and roughly when you signed up. If you use “Send feedback to the developer”, the email body automatically includes the app version, OS version, device manufacturer and model, and app language; you can delete them before sending. If you send feedback inside the app, we store in Cloud Firestore the type you chose (bug, idea or other), your message, an email address for a reply if you enter one, the app version, OS version, device model and app language unless you turn this off, and whether you were signed in. Your leave records and memos are not sent.

How we collect it

You enter it in the app; we receive it from the sign-in provider when you sign in or link a sign-in method; it is generated while you use the app; you send it by email; or you send feedback in the app. The first time you sign in with Kakao, Kakao shows an “app connection” screen; if you connect, Kakao provides your member number to DayOff Mate. Disconnecting the app on the Kakao, Naver or Google side does not delete your DayOff Mate account, so please delete your account in the app or as described on the account deletion page.

3. Information processed only on your phone

The following stays on your phone (or in your own Google account). The developer cannot receive or see it.

  • Records of users who do not sign in: everything in section 2.1.
  • Calendar events: if you turn on “Add days off to calendar” or “Show calendar events”, the app reads and writes your phone's calendar on the phone only. Events are never sent to or stored on our servers, and never included in groups, usage statistics, crash reports or backups. Events the app adds are titled just “Day off” (no leave type); notes are added only if you turn on “Include notes” (never for health leave). By default events go into a “DayOff Mate” calendar that exists only on this phone. If you choose a calendar from another account such as Google, those events sync with that service under its policy.
  • Google Drive auto-backup (if you turn it on): your records are saved in a hidden, app-only space (the app data folder) in your own Google Drive, sent directly from your phone to your Drive without passing through our servers. The developer cannot receive or see them. One file per day is kept for the last 14 days; a file contains your hire date, leave settings, leave records (including notes) and day adjustments. It also contains your work schedule, personal schedule, company calendar, half-day hours and comp time (including extra shifts and events), and, if you entered them, your spouse's childbirth date (for statutory leave deadlines), your home area for weather and your trip destinations. Exported backup files contain the same (the childbirth date, home area and destinations are not stored in your account, only on your phone and in backups). The Google account email used for backup is stored only on your phone, and may be included in operating-system backups if “Phone backups” below is on. See section 4.
  • Exported backup files: saved or sent to the place you choose (phone storage, your cloud, a messenger). Files contain your hire date, records and notes, so do not send them to others.
  • Home widgets: your remaining leave and upcoming days off (dates and leave types, including health leave) are built on the phone and shown on the home screen, and are not sent to the server. Others can see your home screen, so remove the widget if you don't want this. The shift calendar widget shows the month's shift types, extra shifts, leave, holidays and event titles in the same way.
  • Apple Watch: the iPhone app sends your remaining leave, upcoming days off, time left until you leave or start work, and today's and upcoming shifts directly to your paired Apple Watch (Apple's WatchConnectivity) for the watch app and complications. This does not go through our servers.
  • Your own leave and expiry reminders: scheduled on the phone. The same goes for event reminders (the evening before or that morning).
  • Invite QR scanning: the camera image is used on the phone only to read the QR code and is not saved or sent.
  • Leave-pay estimate: the pay you enter (monthly, annual or hourly) to estimate pay for unused leave is used on the phone only for the calculation and is never saved. It is not sent to our servers, groups, usage statistics or crash reports, is not included in any backup (Google Drive auto-backup, backup files or phone backups), and is erased when you close the screen. While this screen is open, Android blocks screenshots and the recent-apps preview.
  • Estimated pay: the hourly pay, extra-shift rate, night and holiday premiums and fixed monthly allowance you enter on the Work tab to estimate pay for extra, night and holiday work are stored only on this phone. They are not stored in your account (on our servers), not sent to groups or crash reports, and not included in Google Drive auto-backup or backup files. Usage statistics record only whether the night premium, holiday premium and fixed allowance are on, never amounts. They are also left out of Android auto-backup and device-to-device transfer; on iPhone, the operating system's iCloud or computer backups may include them along with other app data. You need to enter them again on another phone, and they are erased when you delete all records or the app.
  • Phone backups: if Android auto-backup or device-to-device transfer is on, the operating system may copy the app's records to your Google account backup or a new phone. On iPhone, iCloud or computer backups may include the app's data. This is an operating-system feature; the developer has no access.

4. Google user data (Google API Services User Data Policy)

  • Scope requested: when you turn on Google Drive auto-backup, the app requests only https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.appdata. This scope only gives access to the hidden app folder DayOff Mate creates; the app cannot see or change any other files in your Drive. Google sign-in receives only basic profile information such as your account identifier and email.
  • Use: only to save backup files, list backups with their record counts, restore a backup you choose, and delete backups older than 14 days. Google sign-in information is used only to identify and manage your account.
  • Transfer and sharing: Drive data moves only between your phone and your Google Drive. It is not sent to the developer's servers or to any third party, not used for advertising, marketing, credit assessment or sale, and not read by humans. It is not used to develop, improve or train generalized AI or machine-learning models.
  • Limited Use: DayOff Mate's use and transfer to any other app of information received from Google APIs will adhere to the Google API Services User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements.
  • Turning off and deleting: turn off auto-backup in the app under Settings > Backup (files already saved stay in your Drive). Delete saved files in Google Drive on the web: Settings > Manage apps > DayOff Mate > Options > “Delete hidden app data”. Revoke access in your Google Account under Third-party apps & services.

5. Retention and deletion

We delete personal information without delay once its purpose is fulfilled or its retention period ends. When you delete your account, your account data on the server is deleted without delay; the items below are deleted automatically after the periods shown.

Retention periods
InformationRetention
Account, leave settings, records, group dataUntil you delete your account
Individually deleted records and adjustmentsKept as a “deleted” marker so other phones learn of the deletion; permanently removed within 30 days
Accounts that signed in but did not finish sign-upDeleted immediately if you choose “Not now” or “I'm under 14” on the sign-up screen. An account left without finishing sign-up (for example, because you closed the app on the sign-up screen or a network problem prevented deletion) is deleted automatically after 24 hours
Invite codes and links / ID invitations / pending join requestsDeleted after 48 hours / 14 days / 7 days
Plans, answers to plans, plan linksDeleted automatically within 7 days after the last candidate date; deleted immediately when the organizer deletes the plan or their account
Rate-limit counters for the invite and plan web pages (a hash of the IP address)Expire 24 hours after the last request and are deleted automatically within 24 hours after expiry
Group activity log, records of removed membersDeleted after 30 days
Device push tokensDeleted on sign-out or account deletion, or when the token becomes invalid
Retry data for unlinking Kakao (Kakao member number)Kept only if unlinking Kakao failed during account deletion; the server retries and deletes it once unlinking succeeds (up to 30 days)
Server access and error logs (Google Cloud Logging)30 days
One-time sign-in valuesExpire within 5 minutes and are deleted automatically within 24 hours after expiry
Rate-limit counters (a hash of the installation ID)Expire 24 hours after the last sign-in attempt and are deleted automatically within 24 hours after expiry
Server backups for disaster recoveryUp to 7 days
Firebase Authentication recordsRemoved from Google's backup systems within 180 days after account deletion (access IP logs: a few weeks)
Crash reports (Crashlytics)90 days
Usage statistics (Google Analytics)The retention period set in Google Analytics (up to 14 months)
Firebase installation IDPer Google Firebase policy; removed from Google's systems within 180 days after a deletion request
Inquiry and deletion-request emails1 year after the request is handled
In-app feedback (message, reply email, app info)Deleted automatically 1 year after we receive it. The feedback rate-limit record (a hash of the IP address) is used for 1 hour and deleted within 24 hours

No information currently has to be kept under other laws. If paid features are introduced and records such as payment history must be kept, we will update this policy.

How we delete: data is deleted by server functions (automatic expiry policies and the account-deletion function) when its period ends or when you ask; electronic files are deleted so they cannot be recovered. We keep no paper records. Information that exists only on your phone can be deleted with “Delete all records” in the app or by uninstalling the app.

6. Sharing with third parties and group visibility

The developer does not provide or sell your personal information to third parties, except where required by law or requested by investigative authorities through legal procedures.

Groups show information to members of the same group based on the consent you give when you first create or join a group (“I agree to show the information above to members of this group”).

Group visibility

With “Show my shift schedule”, each day's day off or shift type (with the shift types' names and colors, up to 10) from January 1 of last year to December 31 two years ahead. Seeing days off together, finding common days off, group leave notifications Until you leave or are removed, or the group or your account is deleted

Shift times, extra shifts, events and estimated pay are never shared either, and turning off “Show my shift schedule” deletes the schedule you shared with that group.

  • If a member turns on group leave notifications, the information you share may also appear in their phone notifications (including the lock screen).
  • After you leave a group or it is deleted, information may remain briefly in other members' app caches.
  • While “Let others find me by ID” is on (the default), people who know your exact ID can find and invite you. You can turn it off in Settings.
  • When you invite via KakaoTalk or the share sheet, your nickname, the group name and the invite code or link are sent by you through the app you choose.

Planning a get-together: anyone with the plan link sees the plan name, length, candidate dates and time range, how many people answered, how many people are free in each time slot, and the time that was set. The names of people who answered and each person's available times are shown only to the organizer. The organizer sends the plan link through the app they choose.

9. Advertising and behavioral information

The app (Android and iOS) shows one Google AdMob ad card labeled “Ad” below the records on the Home tab and one at the bottom of the Work tab. The year-end review shows a rewarded ad only when you tap “Watch an ad to open” (at most once a day). The Together tab, other screens and widgets have no ads. The iOS app does not ask for tracking permission (App Tracking Transparency), so it does not use the advertising identifier (IDFA) and requests only non-personalized ads. To show ads, the Google Mobile Ads SDK built into the app sends the following information to Google LLC.

Behavioral information used for ads
Company that processes itGoogle LLC (Google AdMob)
ItemsDevice identifiers (Android: advertising ID and app set ID; iOS: app- or developer-bounded device identifiers), ad impressions and clicks, app use such as app launches and their times, device and OS information, IP address (may be used to estimate approximate location), ad SDK diagnostics
HowSent automatically by the Google Mobile Ads SDK while you use the app
PurposesServing ads, frequency capping, measuring ad performance, preventing click fraud, and (on Android, where permitted) personalized ads
RetentionPer Google's policies
How to refuseOn Android, delete or reset your advertising ID in your phone settings under Privacy (or Google) > Ads. The iOS app does not request personalized ads. In regions where consent is required, such as Europe, a Google consent form appears when you first open the app, and you can choose again under Settings > About > Ad privacy settings in the app. In other regions (including Korea) the Android app has no menu to turn off personalized ads.

The developer does not use this information to identify you and does not use sensitive behavioral information such as health for ads (ad requests contain no records such as leave types or notes). See how Google uses information for ads.

11. Your rights and how to exercise them

You may at any time ask to access, correct, delete or stop processing your personal information, and withdraw consent.

  • In the app: edit leave settings (Settings > My leave info), change your nickname or turn off finding by ID (Settings > Account > “Signed in with …”), change your sharing level or leave a group (Group settings), delete records (Settings > Data > Delete all records), delete your account (Settings > Account > “Signed in with …” > Delete account), link or unlink sign-in methods (Settings > Account > “Signed in with …” > Sign-in methods), turn off usage statistics (Settings > About > Send usage statistics).
  • By email: write to ejok9194@gmail.com. After verifying your identity we will act without delay (within 10 days) and tell you the result. Account deletion requests are handled within 7 days as described on the account deletion page.
  • You may also act through a legal representative or an authorized person; we may ask for a power of attorney.
  • If the law requires us to refuse or limit a request, we will tell you why.
  • The app's leave calculation is done on your phone for your reference; the developer makes no automated decisions about you.

12. Children under 14

People under 14 cannot sign up (sign in). If you choose “I'm under 14” on the sign-up screen, the sign-in information received is deleted immediately (if it cannot be deleted because of a network problem, it is handled like “accounts that did not finish sign-up” in section 5). You can still use the record features without signing in; in that case no personal information is collected other than the automatically generated information in section 2.4. If we learn that we have collected personal information from a child under 14, we delete it without delay.

13. Security measures

  • Administrative: minimizing the information processed (e.g. only the member number from Kakao); access to admin consoles limited to the developer
  • Technical: encryption in transit (HTTPS/TLS) and at rest (Google Cloud default encryption); security rules so only you can read your data and only members can read group data; server rules that reject notes or health-leave types in shared data; App Check so only the genuine app can make requests; rate limits on sign-in, invite codes and ID search; support for hiding notification content on the lock screen
  • Physical: servers and data are protected by the physical security of Google's data centers (processor)

14. Cookies and similar technologies

The app does not use cookies; it uses the device identifiers in section 2.4 (Firebase installation ID, Crashlytics installation ID, app instance ID, advertising ID). You can turn off usage statistics in the app and reset the advertising ID in your phone settings. This website (blessingq.github.io/dayoffmate) uses no cookies or visitor tracking. The plan answer web page also uses no cookies; it keeps only the edit key and name described in section 2.3.1 in your browser's storage. You can delete them by clearing the site data in your browser; after that, answers sent from that browser can no longer be changed (you can ask the organizer to remove them).

16. Changes to this policy

If we change this policy, we will announce it on this page and in the app at least 7 days before it takes effect (30 days for changes that significantly affect your rights). Earlier versions and the period each applied are listed under “Change history” below, and when important content changes we also publish a table comparing it before and after. The full text of earlier versions is available under “Previous versions” below, or by email on request.

  • Published: November 27, 2026 · Effective: November 28, 2026 (adds estimated pay stored only on the phone, sync and backup of extra shifts and events, showing your shift schedule to groups, event reminders, the shift calendar widget and Apple Watch). We first planned December 4, 2026, but moved it earlier because the app version with these features (1.1.0) came out on November 28, 2026. Nothing changes to your disadvantage: estimated pay is now kept only on the phone, and showing your shift schedule applies only to groups where you turn it on
  • This policy is written in Korean. If the English translation differs, the Korean version prevails.

Change history

  • Effective November 28, 2026 (current version, published November 27, 2026; moved up from December 4): states that the hourly pay and allowances you enter for estimated pay on the Work tab are stored only on the phone, never on our servers, in groups or in backups. If you sign in, extra shifts and events are also stored in your account and included in backups, and turning on “Show my shift schedule” for a group shows that group each day's shift type. Also describes event reminders, the shift calendar widget and the Apple Watch app. The changes are in the first table below.
  • Effective November 25, 2026 (applied through November 27, 2026): added planning a get-together (find a time with friends) and sending feedback and bug reports inside the app. If you sign in, your work schedule, personal schedule, company calendar, half-day hours and comp time are also stored in your account so they carry over to a new phone, and Google Drive auto-backup and backup files now also include these plus the spouse's childbirth date and weather areas. The changes are in the second table below.
  • Effective November 23, 2026: applied through November 24, 2026. Updated to match how the app actually works. It describes the full service DayOff Mate provides, including sync, groups and notifications. The changes are listed in the third table below.
  • Effective November 22, 2026 (first version): applied through November 22, 2026

Planning a get-together (sections 1, 2.3.1 and 6)NoneA signed-in organizer creates a plan, and people with the link submit a name and available times (30-minute slots) on the web. Anyone with the link sees only how many answered and how many are free in each slot; names and each person's times are shown only to the organizer
Retention (section 5)-Plans, answers and links are deleted automatically within 7 days after the last candidate date. Rate-limit counters for the invite and plan web pages (a hash of the IP address) expire 24 hours after the last request and are deleted within 24 hours after that

The rate-limit record (a hash of the IP address) is used for 1 hour and deleted within 24 hours
